text: Proof nets (Girard 1987) are a graphical presentation of proof theory for linear logic that:
choices: make the geometry of proof explicit, identifying proofs that are 'the same' up to spurious sequence
explanation: Proof nets: a planar graph representing a linear logic proof. The correctness criterion (Danos-Regnier) identifies when a graph is a valid net. They quotient out permutation of rules.
